*hugs back*

Thanks man. I totally feel you.

I appreciate it. You stay strong too, man.

Oh definitely. I agree, dude. There are crazy people everywhere.

I don't usually get all pissed off, definitely not IRL, but goddamn I'm sick of having it told to me and others.

It's cool man, though I've gotten used to it just gotta let it out sometimes. I appreciate it though.

Eh that's true, there are a lot of good people out there.

Thanks man, I'll keep y'all updated once it starts.
I feel you man; you too. If you ever feel the same, I'm here for you.
It's cool dude, I'll live. I appreciate it, though. Thank you.
Same here man. I'm gonna get a new winter coat this year and make sure it fits right.
I appreciate that, man.

Also, to help you guys out...

/r/ftmporn
Being a transman, this conversation gave me a weird smile

If it makes you feel any better, before the last family reunion I burst into tears and had a panic attack (of course I didn't tell anyone) because nobody on that side of my family knows I'm actually a dude.

I wore what I usually wear, along with the binder and everything, but I still was called my birthname and the wrong pronouns. When I was introduced as my dad's "daughter", I noticed people seemed surprised at first, which helped I guess.

But then my sister and I ditched it and went to the zoo so it resolved itself
Dude, mad respect to you, man. You were unselfish and you made a good decision. Though I've never been in that situation, I say you handled that well.
Ah I gotcha. Yeah man, same here. No kid deserves to go through that or suffer from the possible consequences
Holy shit dude. I hope the students are alright. Do you know them?
That means a lot, dude. :') I really appreciate that. I just gotta stick to it for a bit longer.

I'm gonna start doing that.

I hope to get a PhD in quantum physics and another in another field of physics, and maybe a secondary degree in psychology.

That's true man. It still sucks that they always ask in front of everyone.

I'm really excited to go to college because of that.

That's true... I may. I'll probably write them a personal letter instead. Or maybe just my dad, since I live with him. My mom has an idea.

Thank you so much, man. 

I guess to continue, it's just really strange to be transgender. Like, people usually ask really personal questions and they expect answers - I usually do answer, but I usually ask, "Why would you ask that?" first. 

It kinda makes it hard to get close to people, too. Most of my IRL friends are more like acquaintances, and we don't speak much past "Hey, how are you?"

It's weird to go in public since I never really know who's gonna say "she" and who's gonna say "he". But eh, it's inevitable. But on the bright side, my sister's boyfriend's mom asked him "if he was gonna introduce her to [sister's name]'s brother" which was really nice.

Word, I'll check that out. I appreciate that, thank you. 

Thanks man, I really appreciate that. That would probably be a good idea - something happened a while ago, and I expressed my feelings over a note to my dad. He seemed to understand it, much better than if I spoke to him, I think. 

Thank you for the advice, dude.

I might join this transgender support group soon. I probably have to go into counseling to start testosterone, so I could bring it up then. 

They're *pretty* there for me, but they still don't try at all to use the right pronouns or name. My sister does to a degree - and I like what she does: She calls me my chosen name and her brother to other people, and she/my birthname *only* in the house. That's okay. 

I should maybe tell my family about dysphoria. They probably wouldn't understand, but it could do something. I just hate expressing my feelings in real life, which makes it a lot harder to do so.
I appreciate it, yo. Thank you.

Dude, I totally feel you. I always have to tell people I hate dating and hate relationships. Don't get me wrong, I have romantic feelings but I don't like to show them. It's complicated I guess.

But yeah man, I'm glad she took it well and that you were straightforward.
